exposure: initial postnatal 24-hour clinical characteristics (surfactant use, dopamine use, first 24-hour intravenous fluid amount)
cohort: The study included 682 preterm infants with a median gestational age of 31 weeks (IQR: 28-34 weeks) and a median birth body weight of 1360 g (IQR: 1085-1861 g).
finding: For very low birth body weight neonates, surfactant use, dopamine use, and the amount of first 24-hour intravenous fluid predicted the requirement of PDA treatment and surgical ligation, while for neonates with birth body weight >=1500g, placenta previa, lower birth body weight, and systolic blood pressure predicted the risk and response to PDA treatment.
birth_weight: Median 1360 g (IQR: 1085-1861 g), including very low birth body weight (VLBW) neonates and neonates with BBW >=1500 g.
